articles.title: FIBA Women's World Cup 2026 Team USA: What is the United States Women's National Basketball Team roster?
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Breanna Stewart headline a 12-player squad chasing another gold medal in Berlin
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Breanna Stewart headline a 12-player squad chasing another gold medal in Berlin
articles.body:
Team USA will arrive in Berlin without A’ja Wilson or Kelsey Plum , but the United States still has the kind of roster depth that makes anything short of another gold medal feel like a disappointment.

The Americans open the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup against China on Friday, September 4, beginning their pursuit of a fifth consecutive title.

They have won nine of the past 12 editions of the tournament and remain the standard everyone else is trying to catch.

The final roster blends established champions such as Breanna Stewart, Chelsea Gray and Napheesa Collier with a younger group led by Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese .

Wilson and Plum were ruled out shortly before the tournament because of health reasons, leading USA Basketball to add Washington Mystics teammates Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen .

“The makeup of this roster is pretty straightforward,” USA Basketball managing director Sue Bird said. “I wanted to have a mixture of people with experience, a good mixture of people with youth.”

Bird added: “That sets us up for the future, as well. But also a team that complements each other and can go on the court and win gold. That is always the north star in all of these decisions that I've made.”

Team USA roster for 2026 FIBA Women’s World Cup

Paige Bueckers — Dallas Wings

Caitlin Clark — Indiana Fever

Chelsea Gray — Las Vegas Aces

Rhyne Howard — Atlanta Dream

Sonia Citron — Washington Mystics

Jackie Young — Las Vegas Aces

Kahleah Copper — Phoenix Mercury

Angel Reese — Atlanta Dream

Breanna Stewart — New York Liberty

Kiki Iriafen — Washington Mystics

Aliyah Boston — Indiana Fever

That construction gives Team USA considerable flexibility. Clark and Gray provide elite playmaking, Bueckers can operate on or off the ball, while Howard and Young give the Americans size and shooting in the backcourt.

Stewart and Collier bring championship experience and two-way versatility, Reese adds rebounding and physicality, and Boston gives the roster a reliable interior presence.

Team USA’s path through Berlin

The United States has been drawn into Group D with China, Italy and Czechia .

Group play runs through September 7, followed by quarterfinal qualification games on September 8 and 9. The quarterfinals take place September 10, with the semifinals scheduled for September 12 and the medal games on September 13.

The WNBA paused its season from August 31 through September 17 to accommodate the tournament.

Wilson ’s absence removes the MVP of the 2022 World Cup, but Team USA still has more high-end talent than virtually any opponent it will face.

The more interesting question is how quickly that talent comes together.

With Clark, Bueckers and Reese stepping into larger international roles alongside veterans such as Stewart, Gray and Collier , this tournament could offer both a title run and a preview of the next era of USA Basketball.

articles.title: A'ja Wilson's withdrawal from the FIBA World Cup may have a secret motive: to “steal” the MVP award from Caitlin Clark
articles.standfirst: Rachel DeMita has suggested Wilson's decision could be about preserving her body for the WNBA playoffs and another MVP campaign
articles.summary: Rachel DeMita has suggested Wilson's decision could be about preserving her body for the WNBA playoffs and another MVP campaign
articles.body:
A'ja Wilson 's decision to withdraw from Team USA's 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup squad has generated plenty of discussion, particularly because the Las Vegas Aces superstar remains in the middle of another outstanding WNBA season.

USA Basketball announced Monday that Wilson and Kelsey Plum would miss the tournament in Berlin for health reasons. Washington Mystics players Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron were subsequently added to the roster.

Plum's absence is relatively straightforward to understand. The Phoenix Mercury guard was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the WNBA season because of a lower-leg injury after spending significant portions of the campaign dealing with physical problems.

Wilson's situation is less clear publicly, and that has opened the door to speculation about why the four-time WNBA MVP chose to remain with the Aces rather than pursue another international championship.

Rachel A. DeMita was among those to question whether there could be a strategic element to Wilson's decision.

Speaking during a recent broadcast, DeMita acknowledged that Wilson's official explanation was health-related but suggested that preserving her body for the final stretch of the WNBA campaign could have been a major consideration.

“ Kelsey Plum and A’ja Wilson have actually backed out of playing for Team USA in this FIBA World Cup,” DeMita noted. “Both of them said that the reasoning was due to health reasons.”

She then distinguished Wilson's circumstances from Plum's more visible injury situation.

“Now, A’ja, we don’t know. We haven’t seen A’ja visibly be dealing with anything, and so I personally think that A’ja’s not playing with Team USA because she wants to focus on the W season,” DeMita argued. “She wants to make sure her body is good. She doesn’t want to have to go through more wear and tear again right before the playoffs.”

That theory does not necessarily mean Wilson's decision was motivated by the desire to deny Caitlin Clark an MVP award. Rather, the implication is that Wilson may be prioritizing the individual and team goals immediately ahead of her.

Wilson has plenty to play for with the Aces

The timing is particularly significant because Wilson is attempting to accomplish something that would further cement her place among the WNBA's greatest players.

She has already won four MVP awards, including each of the last two. The official WNBA GM survey conducted before the 2026 season identified Wilson as the overwhelming preseason favorite for the award, with 60% of general managers selecting her.

Wilson has continued to justify those expectations. She is averaging 26.0 points and 9.4 rebounds per game, while also contributing 3.2 assists and maintaining an elite defensive presence.

DeMita believes the stakes extend beyond the individual award.

“I think A’ja is gunning for another MVP trophy and another Finals, like they want to go back-to-back-to-back,” DeMita claimed. “The Aces want to win again, and I don’t blame her in a sense, either.”

That argument carries some weight when considering Las Vegas' position. The Aces are firmly in the playoff picture, and Wilson's availability will be central to their attempt to make another championship run.

The WNBA's schedule has also created an unusual challenge. The regular season is paused from Aug. 31 through Sept. 16 because of the World Cup, meaning players participating for Team USA face another demanding international tournament before returning to their clubs for the final portion of the regular season and playoffs.

Wilson , meanwhile, gets an opportunity to use that period to recover rather than add several high-intensity international games to her workload.

There is also an important distinction between speculation and established fact. Neither Wilson nor USA Basketball has publicly stated that winning another WNBA MVP was the reason for her withdrawal.

The official explanation remains health-related, and reports indicate that Wilson has been carrying a significant workload this season. The Associated Press reported that she needed the opportunity to rest and prepare for the postseason after playing a major role for Las Vegas.

Team USA must now adjust without its biggest interior star

The Americans will enter the World Cup without one of the most accomplished players in international basketball. Wilson was named MVP of the 2022 World Cup and also earned the outstanding-player award at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

Her absence changes the way Team USA will play. Iriafen provides another powerful interior option, while Citron adds versatility and perimeter depth.

FIBA noted that Iriafen previously appeared for the United States during the World Cup qualifying tournament, while Citron is set to make her senior World Cup debut.

Caitlin Clark will remain one of the most closely watched players on the American roster, particularly because her presence gives the tournament another major storyline.

However, Wilson's decision should not automatically be interpreted as an attempt to influence Clark's MVP chances.

The more straightforward explanation is that Wilson has a rare opportunity to protect her body during the league's most important stretch.

For a player chasing another MVP, another championship and potentially another chapter in an already historic career, that could prove to be the most valuable use of the World Cup break.

And if Wilson returns refreshed and leads Las Vegas deep into the postseason, DeMita's theory about the bigger picture may look considerably more plausible, even if there is no evidence that Wilson's decision was specifically made to “steal” the MVP award from Clark.

articles.title: What does FIBA stand for and how many countries will participate in the Women's Basketball World Cup?
articles.standfirst: The 2026 tournament features an expanded 16-nation field in Berlin.
articles.summary: The 2026 tournament features an expanded 16-nation field in Berlin.
articles.body:
FIBA is the international governing body for basketball, but its name comes from the organization's original French title rather than its modern English name.

FIBA originally stood for Federation Internationale de Basketball Amateur , which translates to International Amateur Basketball Federation.

The organization later removed "Amateur" from its official name in 1989, becoming the International Basketball Federation, but the familiar FIBA acronym was retained.

It oversees major international basketball competitions, including the men's and women's World Cups and basketball tournaments connected with the Olympic Games.

How many teams are in the Women's Basketball World Cup?

The 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup will feature 16 national teams when it takes place in Berlin, Germany, from September 4 through September 13.

That represents an expansion from the 12 teams that competed at the previous edition in Sydney in 2022.

FIBA says the move to 16 teams reflects the increasing popularity of women's international basketball.

Germany qualified automatically as the host nation, while Australia, Belgium, Nigeria and the United States secured direct qualification by winning their respective continental championships in 2025.

The remaining places were decided through qualifying tournaments.

Which countries qualified for the 2026 World Cup?

The final field consists of Australia, Belgium, China, Czechia, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Japan, Korea, Mali, Nigeria, Puerto Rico, Spain, Turkiye and the United States.

Those 16 countries have been divided into four groups of four for the opening stage.

Group winners advance directly to the quarterfinals, while teams finishing second and third play an additional qualification game for a place in the last eight. The bottom team in each group is eliminated.

That expanded format means the 2026 Women's Basketball World Cup will be the largest edition since FIBA moved away from the previous 12-team format.

So while FIBA's name dates back to the organization's amateur roots, its flagship women's tournament continues to evolve, with 16 countries now competing for the world championship in Berlin.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers is accused of disrespecting the United States for her viral gesture before the World Cup
articles.standfirst: A playful Team USA video has sparked criticism of the Dallas Wings star days before her World Cup debut
articles.summary: A playful Team USA video has sparked criticism of the Dallas Wings star days before her World Cup debut
articles.body:
P aige Bueckers has found herself at the center of an unexpected controversy just days before making her FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup debut for Team USA .

The Dallas Wings guard appeared in a viral social-media video posted by Angel Reese , where several members of the American roster were dancing and joking around while wearing their Team USA jerseys.

What was intended as a lighthearted moment quickly drew criticism online, with some fans accusing Bueckers of disrespecting the national team uniform.

Bueckers became the focus of the reaction after footage showed her upside down against a wall while twerking. The clip, taken from Reese's TikTok video, spread across social media after being reposted on X by an account covering the Wings.

The reaction has centered less on what Bueckers actually did than on where she did it and what she was wearing.

Some fans argued that a Team USA jersey carries a level of symbolism that makes certain behavior inappropriate, particularly immediately before a major international tournament.

There is, however, no indication that USA Basketball has determined Bueckers violated any team rule or that officials intend to discipline her over the video.

The controversy comes at an especially prominent moment for Bueckers . The former UConn superstar is preparing to play in her first senior World Cup after helping Team USA win at the youth level.

FIBA lists Bueckers among the American players making their World Cup debut in Berlin alongside Reese and Caitlin Clark .

Team USA opens the tournament against China on Friday, Sept. 4, before facing Italy and Czechia in Group D. The Americans enter the competition chasing an unprecedented fifth consecutive World Cup championship.

That pursuit has already become more complicated.

Team USA enters the World Cup with added pressure

The Americans lost two of their biggest stars before the tournament. A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum withdrew because of health issues, forcing coach Kara Lawson to make changes to the roster. Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen received the call to replace them.

That leaves Bueckers with an even more important role as Team USA attempts to maintain its remarkable international dominance.

The 2026 roster was originally packed with established stars and rising talent. Alongside Bueckers , the group included Clark , Reese, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Chelsea Gray, Kahleah Copper and Rhyne Howard .

The combination gave the Americans considerable experience despite the presence of several first-time World Cup players.

The timing of the social-media controversy has therefore added another storyline to an already closely watched tournament.

Bueckers and Reese have previously found themselves involved in an online controversy together. During WNBA All-Star Weekend, the pair appeared in a video discussing a joking $400 wager connected to a Wings-Dream game.

The WNBA subsequently removed the post and reminded the players that conversations about betting on league games can create problems under its gambling policies.

“If y’all win, you get your 400,” Reese appears to say before adding that if Atlanta wins, “you owe me 400.” Bueckers later appeared to feign confusion when asked about the exchange.

The league subsequently explained its decision to remove the video.

“While the social media post was intended to be lighthearted, WNBA players are well aware of the league’s policies prohibiting betting on WNBA games and receive training every year reinforcing those policies,” it read.

“We recognized that the post missed the mark, removed it shortly after it was published, and addressed the matter internally. We will also use this as an opportunity to reemphasize with the players involved that conversations about wagering on WNBA games, even when intended as a joke, can have negative consequences.”

The latest incident is considerably different. Unlike the wagering controversy, there is no indication that Bueckers broke a gambling rule or committed a violation that would trigger league discipline.

Still, the reaction highlights the unusual scrutiny surrounding Team USA athletes. Wearing the national jersey places players in a highly visible role, and fans can interpret even casual social-media moments through that lens.

Bueckers herself has already embraced the significance of representing the United States. Her selection followed an impressive rise from UConn star to WNBA standout, and she now enters her first senior World Cup alongside Clark and Reese as part of the next generation of American stars.

The U.S. also faces a more competitive international field than it has in recent years. FIBA expects France, Belgium and Spain to challenge the Americans, while Team USA's opening group includes China, Italy and Czechia.

For now, the viral clip remains a social-media controversy rather than a basketball story. There has been no public announcement of punishment, and Bueckers remains part of Lawson's roster as the Americans prepare for Friday's opener. Once the ball goes up in Berlin, the focus will quickly shift back to the court.

For Bueckers , that may be the easiest way to answer the criticism: by helping Team USA continue its pursuit of another world championship.

articles.title: When is Team USA playing in the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup?
articles.standfirst: The U.S. opens its title defense against China in Berlin before facing Italy and Czechia in group play.
articles.summary: The U.S. opens its title defense against China in Berlin before facing Italy and Czechia in group play.
articles.body:
T eam USA begins its run at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup on Friday, Sept. 4, with a group-stage matchup against China in Berlin.

The tournament runs through Sept. 13 in Germany, bringing together 16 national teams for the biggest women's international basketball competition between the 2024 Paris Olympics and the 2028 Los Angeles Games .

All games will take place in Berlin, with action split between the 14,000-seat Berlin Arena and the 9,000-capacity Max-Schmeling-Halle.

For American viewers, every Team USA game will be available on TNT or TruTV, while all 36 games at the tournament will stream live on HBO Max. NBC Sports reports that TNT and TruTV will carry 17 games overall, including every U.S. contest.

The Americans enter the tournament with enormous expectations. Head coach Kara Lawson 's team is attempting to extend an extraordinary run of success on the international stage.

According to NBC Sports, the U.S. has won 66 consecutive games across Olympic and World Cup competition, with its last defeat coming against Russia in the 2006 World Championship semifinals.

This year's roster also brings together an intriguing mix of established veterans and some of the biggest young stars in women's basketball.

Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese headline the group, with all three entering their first major senior World Cup.

They join veterans including Breanna Stewart, Chelsea Gray, Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper and Jackie Young . Aliyah Boston, Rhyne Howard, Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen round out the 12-player roster.

Team USA's World Cup schedule and how to watch

The opening phase gives the Americans three games in four days, making the schedule a demanding early test.

Friday, Sept. 4 — USA vs. China

Team USA starts against China at 8:15 a.m. Eastern time. The game tips off at 2:15 p.m. local time in Berlin. It is the first opportunity for the new-look American group to establish its rhythm in a tournament where every game carries significance.

Sunday, Sept. 6 — USA vs. Italy

The Americans return to action two days later against Italy. The later start makes this the more convenient game for U.S. viewers, although it also gives the team less recovery time between contests.

Monday, Sept. 7 — USA vs. Czechia

The group stage concludes against Czechia on Sept. 7. The U.S. will then learn its exact route through the knockout rounds based on the final Group D standings. The official FIBA schedule lists the group phase through Sept. 7 before the tournament moves into its final stages.

The three group games are the only Team USA matchups that are currently fixed regardless of results. If the Americans advance, their schedule continues on Sept. 10 in the quarterfinals.

A quarterfinal victory would put Team USA into the semifinals on Sept. 12, followed by either the championship game or third-place game on Sept. 13. FIBA has confirmed those knockout-round dates, but the exact opponents and game slots depend on how the group and qualifying rounds play out.

That format means American fans could potentially see the U.S. play as many as six games in Berlin: three group contests, a quarterfinal, a semifinal and the championship game.

articles.body:
The 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup gets underway with a high-voltage showdown. At Berlin's Max-Schmeling-Halle, the United States and China face off on the opening day of Group D, a clash that brings together two of the teams with the richest history in international women's basketball and that, from the opening tip, will set the tone for the group.

Group D is one of the strongest in the tournament. In addition to the United States and China, it is completed by Czechia and Italy, so no slip-up will come cheap. Starting with a win not only adds to the standings: it provides a psychological edge and puts either of these two powers on the direct path to the next round, in a format where six teams advance from the group stage.

The United States arrives as the mandatory benchmark of women's basketball worldwide. Its 12-player roster brings together some of the most decisive stars on the professional circuit, such as Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese.

China, for its part, comes in with a larger group —17 names in the squad— that combines veteran experience, towering height, and a new generation of talent poised to make the definitive leap.

What time is the USA vs China game in the FIBA Women's World Cup?

The appointment for the first game of the United States Women's Basketball Team is this Friday, September 4, 2026 at 8:15 a.m. Eastern Time, in an arena with a capacity of 9,000 fans.

In the rest of the United States, the game will start at:

Where can you watch Team USA's game in the United States?

The first Team USA game in the Women's Basketball World Cup can be watched live on television on the following channels and streaming services:

Team USA vs China Rosters: offensive power against an interior wall

The great appeal of the game lies in the clash of styles. The United States is betting on a roster of stars spread across every position. On the perimeter are Sabrina Ionescu, Kelsey Plum, Chelsea Gray, Jewell Loyd, and Ariel Atkins, a group of point guards and shooting guards capable of punishing from long range and creating plays.

Up front, the American squad arrives strong with Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper, Kiki Iriafen, Angel Reese, and Breanna Stewart. At point guard, it is locked down by Paige Bueckers, Sonia Citron, Chelsea Gray, Rhyne Howard, Jackie Young, Aliyah Boston, and Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark. It is a team built to impose tempo, run the floor, and deliver suffocating defense.

China responds with its trademark: height. In the paint, Li Yuan and Han Xu stand out, two imposing-sized centers, along with Mingling Chen, Chen Yujie, Zhang Manman, and the very young Zhang Ziyu. Playmaking falls to guards such as Wang Siyu, Yang Shuyu, and Sun Yu; at the forward positions, Xinyu Luo, Saiqi Jia, and Ziting Tang offer a balance between shooting and defensive work.

China’s approach will be to capitalize on its height advantage on the boards and slow the game down to limit the United States’ transition opportunities. The Americans’, by contrast, will be to speed things up, apply pressure, and turn every turnover into easy points.

Players to watch during the game

A'ja Wilson : a benchmark center, capable of dominating inside and out. Her direct matchup with China's height will be one of the key aspects of the game.

Breanna Stewart : a complete-profile forward, with outside shooting and presence in the paint. She is the kind of player who decides close games.

Han Xu : with her wingspan, she is the piece China will try to use to balance the scales on the boards and protect the rim against American attacks.

What's at stake in Group D for qualification

As this is the first matchday, all teams begin with a 0-0 record. However, the importance of this clash is enormous: a U.S. victory would immediately establish it as the clear favorite in Group D, while a Chinese win would be a statement victory on a global scale and a message to the rest of the contenders.

With Czechia and Italy also in the fight, the point differential that comes out of this game could prove decisive when it comes to determining positions and matchups in the following rounds.

Prediction for Team USA's first game at the 2026 FIBA World Cup

The United States starts as the clear favorite thanks to its roster depth, versatility, and accumulated experience in major tournaments. The talent spread across Ionescu, Plum, Stewart, and Wilson offers too many offensive solutions.

China has the tools to make things uncomfortable — its interior size is a real weapon — and it can keep the score close for much of the game if it controls the pace. Even so, the United States' athletic superiority and bench depth should make the difference in the final minutes.

The reasonable bet is a United States victory, with China offering resistance especially in the first half before the Americans pull away.

Whatever the outcome, Berlin will have the privilege of opening Group D with the most enticing matchup of the opening day.

articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark and Team USA begin their title defense against China in Berlin
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and Team USA begin their title defense against China in Berlin
articles.body:
T eam USA 's long-awaited campaign at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup is finally underway, with the Americans facing China in their opening game of the tournament.

The United States entered the competition as the reigning four-time world champion and is attempting to extend an extraordinary run of dominance on the international stage.

The 2026 tournament is being held in Berlin, Germany, from September 4 through September 13, with 16 national teams competing for the world championship.

For Team USA , the first assignment is China, with the Group D matchup scheduled for Friday, September 4.

FIBA lists the game for 12:15 p.m. local time in Berlin at Max-Schmeling-Halle , which translates to 6:15 a.m. Eastern Time, but the correct U.S. broadcast schedule places the tip at 8:15 a.m. ET, or 1:15 p.m. BST in the United Kingdom. CBS Sports lists TNT and HBO Max as the U.S. viewing options.

The game represents the beginning of a demanding group-stage schedule for Kara Lawson 's team.

Team USA was drawn into Group D alongside China, Italy and Czechia, meaning the Americans have three games to establish their position before the tournament moves into the knockout rounds.

China is not an opponent Team USA can afford to overlook. The Chinese national team reached the 2022 World Cup final, where it finished as runner-up to the United States.

FIBA's head-to-head record also illustrates the Americans' historical advantage, with the U.S. entering their latest meeting having won all 15 previous recorded matchups against China.

The matchup is also significant because this Team USA roster represents something of a changing era.

Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese are among the players making their major senior international tournament debuts, while veterans such as Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young provide championship experience.

Team USA's road through Group D

The Americans' roster did undergo two significant changes before the tournament began. A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum withdrew for health reasons, with Washington Mystics players Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron called into the squad as replacements.

Wilson was Team USA's leading scorer at the 2024 Olympics, making her absence particularly notable, while Plum had also been an important member of recent championship teams.

Despite those changes, expectations remain extremely high. Team USA has not lost a World Cup game since falling to Russia in the 2006 semifinals and is seeking its fifth consecutive championship.

FIBA says the Americans' unbeaten run in the competition has stretched across multiple editions, while the roster combines established stars with a new generation of American talent.

Lawson has also acknowledged that the international field has become increasingly competitive.

"The world is improving and has continued to improve, and there's more depth to the teams at the World Cup now," Lawson said this week.

That makes the opening game against China an important early test, particularly for a roster that has not played together extensively at this level.

What is Team USA's next game after China?

Once the Americans complete their opening assignment, their attention will immediately turn toward Italy.

Team USA is scheduled to play Italy on Sunday, September 6, in its second Group D contest. CBS Sports lists that game for 2:45 p.m. ET, with TNT and HBO Max carrying the action in the United States.

The group stage concludes the following day when Team USA meets Czechia on Monday, September 7, also at 2:45 p.m. ET according to the CBS Sports schedule. FIBA's official schedule lists the matchup for 6:45 p.m. local time in Berlin.

The structure of the tournament means the group games carry added importance. The four group winners will advance directly to the quarterfinals, while the teams finishing second and third must go through qualification games on September 8 and 9. The bottom team in each group is eliminated.

The quarterfinals are scheduled for September 10, followed by the semifinals on September 12. The championship game and third-place game will take place on September 13 in Berlin.

For Team USA , the immediate objective is therefore straightforward: navigate China, Italy and Czechia successfully and put itself in the strongest possible position for the knockout phase.

With Clark making her World Cup debut and several other young stars taking on their first major senior tournament, the opening game against China is more than simply the first entry on the schedule.

It is the first opportunity to see whether this new-look American roster can maintain the standard established by the teams that came before it.

- Team USA vs. China: Friday, September 4, 8:15 a.m. ET / 1:15 p.m. BST

- Team USA vs. Italy: Sunday, September 6, 2:45 p.m. ET

- Team USA vs. Czechia: Monday, September 7, 2:45 p.m. ET

- Quarterfinals: Thursday, September 10

- Semifinals: Saturday, September 12

- Final: Sunday, September 13

articles.title: Caitlin Clark launches from deep as Angel Reese refuses to back down from 7-foot-3 Zhang Ziyu in Team USA’s FIBA World Cup rout of China
articles.standfirst: Clark stretched the court, Reese accepted an almost impossible defensive assignment and Paige Bueckers helped turn familiar WNBA opponents into a dominant national team
articles.summary: Clark stretched the court, Reese accepted an almost impossible defensive assignment and Paige Bueckers helped turn familiar WNBA opponents into a dominant national team
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark was already far enough behind the three-point line to make most players reconsider the shot. She never hesitated. The ball left her hands and dropped through the basket, delivering another reminder that the normal boundaries of the court do not always apply to her.

Angel Reese’s defining moment came at the opposite end. She lowered her body, raised her arms and tried to keep China’s 7-foot-3 Zhang Ziyu away from the basket. Reese moved her feet and attempted to absorb the contact without reaching, but the physical battle eventually ended with a foul.

One play showed range. The other showed refusal. Together, they captured how Team USA’s new generation began the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup with a 94-61 victory over China in Berlin.

The United States led 49-29 at halftime and kept increasing the margin until the opening game became a 33-point rout. Clark, Paige Bueckers and Rhyne Howard shared the team lead with 14 points apiece, giving the Americans three different answers whenever China attempted to slow them down.

Clark did not start, a decision that immediately generated questions about head coach Kara Lawson’s rotation . By the final buzzer, however, she had played a game-high 25 minutes and finished with 14 points, 11 assists and no turnovers.

The long three created the highlight, but Clark’s passing caused even more damage. She recorded six assists in only 10 first-half minutes and repeatedly accelerated the offense before China could organize its defense.

Bueckers offered a different kind of control. She scored efficiently, moved without the ball and helped maintain the rhythm of the offense while Clark initially waited on the bench. Howard provided another 14 points, preventing China from concentrating all its defensive attention on the two young guards.

Angel Reese accepts Team USA’s tallest challenge against Zhang Ziyu

Reese’s value was measured less by scoring and more by the assignment she accepted. Zhang, a 19-year-old center who stands approximately a foot taller than Reese, presents a problem few teams can recreate in practice. She can receive the ball close to the rim without jumping and force defenders to decide between surrendering position or risking a foul.

Reese chose to fight. She stayed low, held her ground and tried to make every step difficult for Zhang. The whistle eventually went against her, but the possession revealed the type of physical resistance Team USA will need if it faces another elite interior player later in the tournament.

Zhang still finished with 13 points and six rebounds, but the Americans prevented her from controlling the game. They used speed, defensive pressure and ball movement to attack the areas where China’s enormous height advantage could not protect it.

China also entered the tournament without Dallas Wings center Li Yueru, whose passport was reportedly lost in the mail before she could travel. Li averaged 17.7 points and 11 rebounds at the 2024 Paris Olympics, and her absence deprived China of another experienced interior presence alongside Zhang and Han Xu.

The victory was Team USA’s 70th consecutive win in official competition since losing to Russia in the 2006 World Cup . The Americans have won four consecutive World Cups and 11 titles overall, but many of the players responsible for building that dynasty are no longer present.

Team USA will be back on the court Sunday, September 6, against Italy in its second Group D game at the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup. Tipoff is set for 2:45 p.m. ET, with the game airing on TNT and streaming live on HBO Max. Another victory would move the Americans closer to securing first place in the group before Monday’s finale against Czechia.

Held every four years, the FIBA Women's World Cup has been completely dominated by the United States with 11 titles , capturing gold in every single edition since 1998, aside from a bronze finish in 2006, making them overwhelming favorites to secure their fifth consecutive world championship.

The tournament kicked off with basketball heavyweights like Spain , France , and the United States establishing immediate authority by crushing their respective opening opponents by margins of 30 or more points.

During Team USA's commanding 94-61 victory over China , Caitlin Clark electrified the floor off the bench to capture Player of the Game honors by logging a team-high 25 minutes, dishing out 11 assists , the most by an American player in 28 years, and dropping a game-best 14 points, tied directly with backcourt partner Paige Bueckers .

Paige Bueckers Chemistry With Caitlin Clark on the World Stage

The matchup also generated one of the tournament's most viral talking points when Bueckers was spotted standing next to China's towering 7-foot-3 center Zhang Ziyu , looking up in sheer astonishment.

When questioned after the final buzzer about her growing on-court synergy with Caitlin Clark, the Dallas Wings guard did not hesitate to praise her teammate's impact. "We know how to play well off of each other. She draws so much defensive attention, so a lot of the defense is worried about her and she has great vision as well," Bueckers remarked.

That assessment is entirely backed up by the box score, where Clark's record-setting 11 assists showcased her elite floor-mapping ability.

Because of her lethal perimeter shooting and exceptional ball security, she constantly commands collapsing double-teams, creating easy opportunities for her supporting cast, explaining why she also stands as the leading assist-maker in the current WNBA landscape.

Looking ahead, the road continues this Sunday when Team USA squares off against Italy, a squad fresh off defeating Czechia in their opening fixture. Following the Italian matchup, the Americans will wrap up Group D play on Monday against Czechia.

articles.title: What does Team USA need to qualify for the next round of the FIBA Women's World Cup 2026 and what is the prediction?
articles.standfirst: Team USA has already made a strong start in Berlin, but the new FIBA format means winning Group D is especially valuable as Caitlin Clark, Breanna Stewart and company chase another world title
articles.summary: Team USA has already made a strong start in Berlin, but the new FIBA format means winning Group D is especially valuable as Caitlin Clark, Breanna Stewart and company chase another world title
articles.body:
T eam USA began its 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup campaign exactly as many expected, cruising past China 94-61 in Berlin on Friday.

The result immediately put the Americans in a strong position in Group D, but there is still work to do before they can secure the most favorable route through the knockout stage.

The United States entered the tournament looking for a fifth consecutive World Cup gold medal and an unprecedented continuation of its dominance in the competition.

USA Basketball had already identified the tournament as another opportunity to extend the program's extraordinary run, while ESPN listed the Americans and France among the leading contenders before the tournament began.

The biggest question now is straightforward: what does Team USA actually need to do to advance?

Under FIBA's new competition structure, 16 teams have been divided into four groups of four. Each team plays three group games.

The team finishing first in each group goes directly into the quarterfinals, while the teams finishing second and third must play a single-elimination qualification game for a place in the last eight.

That makes first place significantly more important than simply avoiding elimination.

Team USA is in Group D alongside China, Italy and Czechia. The Americans opened with their 94-61 victory over China, giving them two competition points and an early advantage in the group standings.

Italy also defeated Czechia on opening day, leaving the initial Group D table with the USA and Italy on 1-0 records.

The United States next faces Italy on Sunday before completing group play against Czechia on Monday.

One more win should guarantee Team USA a knockout place

From a qualification standpoint, the simplest path for the Americans is to win either of their remaining games.

A second victory would put Team USA at 2-1 even if it subsequently loses its other matchup. With four teams in the group, a 2-1 record guarantees a finish inside the top three and therefore a place in the knockout phase.

However, the Americans will have a much bigger incentive than simply reaching the next round.

Three wins from three would guarantee first place in Group D, assuming the United States finishes ahead of its rivals on record.

That would send the Americans directly into the quarterfinals and eliminate the additional qualification game that second- and third-place teams must play.

Even a 2-1 record could potentially be enough to win the group depending on the other results and applicable tiebreakers. But Team USA controls its own destiny most cleanly by beating Italy and Czechia.

The opening victory also provided an encouraging glimpse of what the revamped American roster can offer.

Caitlin Clark made her World Cup debut with 14 points and 11 assists, while Rhyne Howard also scored 14 points. Paige Bueckers added 14, giving the United States multiple perimeter threats in a game it eventually won by 33 points.

The result was particularly significant because this is not the exact roster many expected to see when preparations began.

A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum withdrew before the tournament because of health and injury concerns.

Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen were subsequently brought into the group, placing additional responsibility on veterans such as Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier while giving younger players a larger opportunity.

Despite those absences, the United States remains the No. 1-ranked team in the world according to FIBA and entered Berlin as the clear favorite for another championship.

There are legitimate threats elsewhere in the tournament. France is widely viewed as one of the strongest challengers after coming within one point of the Americans in the 2024 Olympic final.

Belgium and Australia are also among the teams capable of making a deep run, while China showed during the opening game that its enormous frontcourt can present unusual challenges even in defeat.

That is why winning Group D could prove particularly important.

Avoiding the qualification round gives the Americans an extra recovery day and removes the possibility of a single-game upset before the quarterfinals.

From there, the tournament becomes a conventional knockout competition, with quarterfinals, semifinals and medal games determining the champion.

Prediction: Team USA should win Group D

The prediction is relatively straightforward after the opening round: Team USA should finish first in Group D and advance directly to the quarterfinals.

The Americans already have a 1-0 record and a significant point differential after beating China. Italy and Czechia still have to navigate their own matchup, while the U.S. has demonstrated that its depth remains considerable despite the absence of Wilson and Plum.

The more interesting question will be what happens once Team USA reaches the quarterfinals.

France appears to be the most obvious threat, while Belgium and Australia could also make the latter stages highly competitive. ESPN's pre-tournament assessment similarly placed the United States and France among the leading favorites.

For now, though, the equation is simple. Beat Italy or Czechia and Team USA should have enough to guarantee a top-three finish. Win both, and the Americans will take the cleanest possible route into the quarterfinals.

Considering the roster's combination of experience, athleticism, playmaking and depth, the safest prediction is that Team USA will do exactly that, win Group D and remain on course for a fifth consecutive FIBA Women's World Cup championship.

articles.standfirst: The defending champions return to action Sunday after opening with a dominant win over China.
articles.summary: The defending champions return to action Sunday after opening with a dominant win over China.
articles.body:
Team USA continues its 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup campaign against Italy on Sunday, September 6, with both teams looking to remain unbeaten in Group D.

The United States opened the tournament with an emphatic 94-61 victory over China , extending its remarkable World Cup winning streak and immediately underlining why it entered Berlin as the favorite.

Italy also began with a victory , defeating Czechia in its opening group game.

What time is USA vs Italy?

USA vs Italy is scheduled to tip off at 8:45 p.m. local time in Berlin on Sunday, September 6.

That means the game begins at 2:45 p.m. ET and 11:45 a.m. PT in the United States. FIBA lists the contest as the third game in Group D and confirms Berlin Arena as the venue.

American viewers can watch the game live on TNT.

The matchup will also be available to stream on HBO Max, giving fans another way to follow Team USA's second appearance of the tournament. Current U.S. television listings also confirm the start on TNT.

Team USA looking to build on dominant opener

The Americans wasted little time making an impression in Berlin.

Caitlin Clark recorded 14 points and 11 assists against China, while Paige Bueckers also scored 14 as the United States cruised to a 33-point victory in its first game.

That result made this Italy matchup another important opportunity for coach Kara Lawson's team to build chemistry before completing the group stage against Czechia.

Italy presents a different challenge after also winning its opener, and FIBA's format makes every group result significant.

The winner of each four-team group advances directly to the quarterfinals, while the teams finishing second and third must go through the qualification round.

Team USA is chasing another world championship after decades of dominance in the competition.

Sunday's game provides the next test, with TNT carrying the action nationally as the Americans look to move to 2-0 in Berlin.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers gets asked by FIBA to explain viral moment with towering Chinese player
articles.standfirst: Bueckers’ reaction to Zhang Ziyu quickly became a moment fans couldn’t stop talking about
articles.summary: Bueckers’ reaction to Zhang Ziyu quickly became a moment fans couldn’t stop talking about
articles.body:
Paige Bueckers has a peculiar sense of humor, and the way she carries herself on the court is always something that gets attention. This time, her reaction was priceless when she had to face a Chinese player who stood several inches taller than her. Team USA faced China in its first game of the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup, knowing the matchup would not be an easy one. They came prepared, but being mentally ready for an opponent is different from experiencing it on the court.

The height difference immediately stole the spotlight. Bueckers appeared just as impressed as the fans by China center Zhang Ziyu, who stands 7-foot-3 compared to Bueckers’ 6-foot frame . The contrast was impossible to miss whenever the two players were near each other.

The height difference had everyone watching

Bueckers appeared to have questions and may have shared some of them with Ziyu, who responded with a smile and leaned down to hear the Wings guard better. Bueckers’ gestures and Ziyu’s reaction quickly became one of the most viral moments from the game . FIBA’s Women’s Basketball World Cup account shared several images of the exchange, including a cartoon version of the two players, and jokingly asked Bueckers to reveal what they had discussed, telling her to “spill the conversation.”

The viral exchange, however, did not overshadow what Bueckers accomplished in her World Cup debut. The Wings guard scored 14 points, tying Caitlin Clark and Rhyne Howard for the team scoring lead, while also adding four assists and two steals. Zhang’s size created challenges that few guards have faced, but Bueckers still looked comfortable on the court.

Bueckers made her impact beyond the viral moment

Her performance helped Team USA establish control early, with the Americans leading 27-14 after the first quarter and holding China to 32 percent shooting for the game. Still, the interaction with Ziyu will likely remain one of the moments fans remember most from the matchup , especially because of how genuine the exchange between the two players appeared to be.

articles.title: Team USA survives a wild finish against Italy after a dramatic fourth quarter
articles.standfirst: A dramatic finish, clutch veterans, and a battle that went down to the final seconds.
articles.summary: A dramatic finish, clutch veterans, and a battle that went down to the final seconds.
articles.body:
Jackie Young scored 10 points and the U.S. survived its toughest test in the women's basketball World Cup in two decades with a 55-52 victory over Italy on Sunday .

The U.S. has won 32 straight World Cup games dating back to a loss to Russia in the 2006 semifinals. Only one team had come within single digits of the Americans before Sunday during this run, when Australia lost by eight in 2010.

The Americans (2-0) had to work hard for this victory, putting up the lowest point total in a preliminary-round game since 1971 , when they had 51 against France.

The U.S. trailed 50-48 with 4:29 left before going on a 7-0 run. Breanna Stewart , who missed her first eight shots, scored her first basket of the game to put the Americans up 51-50. Young then hit a layup after the U.S. got an offensive foul against Italy on its next possession.

The Americans then got another defensive stop and Chelsea Gray hit a jumper to make it a five-point game.

Matilde Villa scored to get Italy back within three with less than a minute to go.

The U.S. had a couple of chances to make it a two-possession lead but couldn't convert.

Italy (1-1) had one last chance to tie it, but Cecilia Zandalasini's 3-pointer was off at the buzzer.

articles.title: Kara Lawson gets 100% real after Caitlin Clark struggles: “You see where your weaknesses are”
articles.standfirst: The superstar had a career-low performance, but veterans Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray stepped up to deliver a dramatic win over Italy and keep the gold medal chase alive.
articles.summary: The superstar had a career-low performance, but veterans Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray stepped up to deliver a dramatic win over Italy and keep the gold medal chase alive.
articles.body:
It was far from a walk in the park for Team USA during its second appearance at the 2026 FIBA Women’s World Cup . In fact, several of the team’s star players, including Caitlin Clark , disappeared from the spotlight, allowing veteran players to step up and rescue an important victory over Italy.

With that scenario in mind, and considering her comments could be interpreted as a message to her players, Team USA head coach Kara Lawson spoke after the 55-52 victory.

What Kara Lawson said after the win over Italy

“In the fourth quarter, when it was winning time, my veterans came through big. Jackie Young was terrific, and Chelsea (Gray) made a huge shot late. Sometimes it’s good to be tested like this. You see where your weaknesses are, and we know exactly what we need to improve,” Lawson said during her interview with TNT Sports.

This is exactly the moment to make adjustments, especially when discussing areas of concern. Caitlin Clark was one of those weaknesses on Sunday. The Indiana Fever star finished 0-for-6 from the field with just one point, a stat line she had never recorded before in either the WNBA or an NCAA game.

With the victory, Team USA improved to 2-0 in the FIBA Women’s World Cup and officially secured a direct spot in the quarterfinals of the knockout stage. Their opponent remains to be determined.

The win also guaranteed that the Americans will be placed on the opposite side of the bracket from France , setting up the possibility of a championship showdown between the two tournament favorites in the final on September 13 .

articles.title: Kara Lawson urged to back Caitlin Clark and bench veterans to get Team USA working better
articles.standfirst: Linda Cohn wants the Team USA coach to mix up her rotations after a narrow win over Italy.
articles.summary: Linda Cohn wants the Team USA coach to mix up her rotations after a narrow win over Italy.
articles.body:
Kara Lawson has been urged to put more faith in Caitlin Clark and move away from relying so heavily on Team USA's veteran players after a difficult 55-52 win over Italy at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup .

The Americans remained unbeaten at 2-0, but the performance was far less convincing than their 94-61 opening victory over China.

Former ESPN anchor Linda Cohn believes Lawson's rotations were a major part of the problem.

"Here's the other criticism I have, and this is probably the bigger one. She stays too long with either her veterans on the floor, or she'll stay too long with the young players on the floor without mixing them up with the veterans," Cohn said.

"She needs to not be afraid to change things up. She was outcoached against Italy, but I believe in Kara Lawson. I believe she'll make the right moves on Monday. She's gonna have to... Don't stay so long with the veterans."

Caitlin Clark could get bigger Team USA role

Clark herself endured a difficult game against Italy.

The Indiana Fever star played 18 minutes and finished with just one point, four rebounds, one assist, two steals and a block.

Despite that performance, Cohn believes Lawson should consider an even bigger change by putting Clark into the starting lineup.

"Would it be the end of the world if you mixed up the starting lineup and for the first time, you put Caitlin Clark in the starting lineup?" Cohn said.

"Because I promise you this: she's not going to have back-to-back one-point performances. She'll be inspired more than ever. Think about that adjustment, because it just might mean everything."

Lawson faces major rotation decision

Lawson began the tournament by leaning on experienced national team players in her starting five, while Clark and several other younger stars came off the bench.

That approach worked comfortably against China, when Clark produced 14 points and 11 assists.

Italy exposed more problems.

Cohn isn't arguing that the veterans should disappear from the rotation entirely. Her criticism is that Lawson needs to blend the two groups more effectively instead of leaving either unit together for too long.

With Team USA still unbeaten, there is time to experiment.

But after escaping Italy by only three points, the pressure is growing on Lawson to find the combination that gets the best out of Clark and the rest of the roster.

articles.title: Team USA fans turn on Angel Reese over controversial World Cup outfit decision
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream star drew criticism after appearing in personal sponsor gear instead of Team USA Nike apparel.
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream star drew criticism after appearing in personal sponsor gear instead of Team USA Nike apparel.
articles.body:
Angel Reese has found herself at the center of another online debate after her clothing choice at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup angered some Team USA fans.

Reese is a Reebok athlete, while Team USA is outfitted by Nike.

That conflict became a talking point when Reese was seen wearing Reebok gear rather than the standard Nike apparel associated with the national team setup.

Some fans viewed the decision as putting an individual sponsorship ahead of the team.

Angel Reese sparks backlash over Team USA outfit

The criticism quickly spread online, with some supporters calling the move "selfish" and questioning why Reese would choose to stand apart from the rest of the roster during an international tournament.

The issue isn't about what Reese wears during games, where uniform requirements are clear.

Instead, the debate centers on appearances away from the court and whether players should prioritize national team branding over personal endorsement deals.

Reese's relationship with Reebok has become a major part of her profile since she entered the WNBA, and the company has invested heavily in making her one of the faces of its basketball revival.

That makes the situation more complicated than simply refusing to wear Team USA gear.

Sponsor conflict creates awkward Team USA debate

Nike's long-standing relationship with USA Basketball means most official apparel carries its branding.

Reese , however, has contractual obligations of her own.

That hasn't stopped fans from questioning the optics.

To critics, every player representing the United States should look unified during a World Cup, particularly when Team USA is already under intense scrutiny over performances and rotations.

Others have defended Reese by pointing out that athletes regularly have individual commercial agreements that can clash with team sponsors.

The debate ultimately highlights a growing tension in modern women's basketball.

Players are building increasingly valuable personal brands, and sponsorship deals now carry far more weight than they did even a few years ago.

Reese is one of the clearest examples of that shift.

Her decision may have irritated some Team USA supporters, but it also shows why managing personal endorsements and national team obligations is becoming an increasingly complicated issue for the sport's biggest stars.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark doesn't like it when people look at her feet in the locker room: her Team USA teammates make fun of her
articles.standfirst: The Team USA star became the center of a playful moment with her teammates.
articles.summary: The Team USA star became the center of a playful moment with her teammates.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark may be one of the most scrutinized players at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup , but even she wasn't prepared for the attention to shift toward her feet.

The Indiana Fever star became the subject of a lighthearted exchange after cameras captured teammates focusing on them.

Clark immediately made clear she wasn't particularly comfortable with everyone looking down.

"Stop looking at my feet," Clark said.

That response only made the situation funnier for the players around her, who quickly burst into laughter.

Caitlin Clark's teammates can't stop laughing

The moment offered a glimpse of the chemistry developing inside Team USA during the tournament.

Clark appeared embarrassed by the sudden attention and tried to shut the conversation down, but her teammates were clearly enjoying her reaction.

The playful exchange quickly gained attention online as fans reacted to a more relaxed side of the national team away from the pressure of international competition.

Clark has been one of the biggest stories surrounding Team USA since joining the roster, with almost every aspect of her performances and interactions attracting attention.

This time, however, there was nothing particularly serious behind it.

Her teammates were simply having fun at her expense.

Team USA chemistry grows during World Cup

The scene came during a tournament in which coach Kara Lawson has been trying to blend an experienced veteran core with several younger stars.

Clark is part of that younger group and has already experienced contrasting performances.

She recorded 14 points and 11 assists in Team USA's dominant opening win over China before being held to just one point against Italy.

That has sparked plenty of debate about Lawson's rotations and Clark's role moving forward.

Away from those discussions, the mood around the team appeared considerably lighter.

The laughter surrounding Clark's plea to stop looking at her feet showed a group comfortable enough to tease one another despite the expectations surrounding them.

Clark might be accustomed to cameras following her everywhere.

But judging by her reaction, having her teammates suddenly focus on her feet is one type of attention she could happily do without.

articles.title: Team USA hit with brutal criticism: "Hard for me to be proud of this, because even the refs are on our side"
articles.standfirst: Rachel DeMita tore into the Americans after their narrow 55-52 escape against Italy.
articles.summary: Rachel DeMita tore into the Americans after their narrow 55-52 escape against Italy.
articles.body:
Team USA remained unbeaten at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup with a 55-52 victory over Italy, but former college basketball player Rachel DeMita was far from impressed.

"It’s hard for me to be proud of this as a USA fan, because even if I’m looking at this game objectively, the refs are on our side," DeMita said.

"Italy came out with spark, with fire, with passion… Did they play perfectly? No, they played far from perfect. Italy had 18 turnovers on the night. They had 12 in the first half, and USA only wins by three?"

DeMita couldn't understand how Team USA failed to take greater advantage.

"You mean to tell me a team turns the ball over 18 times in a game and you win by three? Italy shoots 37% from the field, 37%, and USA only wins by three? Italy shoots 13% from three; they made two threes on the night and, USA wins by three?"

Team USA struggles despite major statistical advantages

The Americans had beaten Italy 93-59 during World Cup qualifying, making Sunday's result even more surprising.

Their 55 points were also Team USA's lowest total in a Women's World Cup game since 1971.

DeMita pointed directly to the free throw and foul numbers as another reason the performance concerned her.

"[Team USA were] not able to capitalize on [Italy] shooting so poorly from the field and from the three-point line, and 70% from the free-throw line," she said.

"Italy had 22 team fouls to USA’s 14. USA shot 10 more free throws than Italy did. Both teams shot 70% from the free-throw line."

Team USA still trailed 50-48 with 4:29 remaining before Chelsea Gray, Jackie Young and Breanna Stewart helped close the game on a 7-0 run.

Kara Lawson delivers her own warning

Coach Kara Lawson was hardly satisfied either.

"Let this be the last time that a team plays with more passion than throughout the course of the game," Lawson told her players afterward.

She then delivered an even stronger message.

"Let this be the last time that all 12 don’t show up to compete at a high level, and then let this be the last time that we lack that resilient mindset because we’re so upset that we’re not scoring the way we normally score."

Team USA escaped with the win. But between DeMita's statistical takedown and Lawson's own warning, nobody around the Americans appeared interested in pretending it was good enough.

articles.title: How many times has Team USA won the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup?
articles.standfirst: The United States has dominated the competition more than any other nation.
articles.summary: The United States has dominated the competition more than any other nation.
articles.body:
Team USA has won the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup 11 times, making the United States the most successful country in the history of the tournament.

The Americans claimed their first title in 1953 and have added championships in 1957, 1979, 1986, 1990, 1998, 2002, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022.

That record puts the United States comfortably ahead of every other country to have won the competition.

How dominant has Team USA been at the World Cup?

The modern run has been particularly impressive.

Team USA has won the last four Women's Basketball World Cups , taking the title in 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022.

The 2022 championship in Sydney was the United States' 11th overall.

That victory also extended a remarkable unbeaten streak in the competition, with the Americans becoming increasingly difficult to challenge during the knockout stages.

Their dominance has been built around a deep pool of WNBA talent, strong defensive play and the ability to rotate elite players without a major drop in quality.

Who else has won the Women's Basketball World Cup?

The Soviet Union remains the next most successful team historically with six titles.

Brazil, Australia and several other nations have also won the tournament, but none has matched the United States' total.

The World Cup has been held since 1953 and is one of the biggest international competitions in women's basketball.

Team USA has therefore won more than a quarter of all editions played.

The United States enters each tournament as one of the clear favorites, and its recent record explains why.

With 11 world championships and four consecutive titles heading into the 2026 edition, Team USA remains the benchmark for the rest of international women's basketball.

If the Americans win again in 2026, they would extend their record to 12 titles and make it five consecutive World Cup championships.

articles.title: Where to watch USA vs Czechia in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup today and what time does the game start?
articles.standfirst: The United States National Team faces the Czech Republic in the final group stage match
articles.summary: The United States National Team faces the Czech Republic in the final group stage match
articles.body:
The FIBA Women's World Cup reaches its third day with a matchup that, in theory, has a very clear favorite. The United States, unbeaten leader of Group D with a 2-0 record, faces a Czech Republic side that has yet to win (0-2) and arrives needing to compete to avoid being backed into a corner.

The numbers in this phase paint the contrast clearly. The United States has averaged solid offensive production—149 points scored and 113 allowed across its two games—a +36 differential that is the highest in the group.

That defensive balance, allowing just over 56 points per game, speaks of a team that not only overwhelms on offense but also clamps down around its own basket.

Czechia, meanwhile, has scored 124 points in favor and 137 against, a -13 differential that leaves it at the bottom of Group D. It’s not that the European team has been unable to score; the problem has been stopping its rivals in decisive moments.

With two straight losses, the Czechs need a perfect game—and a bit of luck—to pull off the upset.

Where is Team USA's third game in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup being played and what time does it start?

The venue for the matchup between Team USA and the Czech Republic will be the Uber Arena in Berlin, Germany, a facility with a capacity of 14,200 spectators, in a game scheduled for this Monday, September 7, 2026, at the following times:

Pacific Time : 11:45 a.m.

This game, like the rest of the matches played in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup 2026, can be watched live on HBO Max.

American talented lineup: depth to spare

The United States roster is a catalog of the WNBA’s best players. On the perimeter, the point guards Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers stand out, both 24 years old, accompanied by the veteran presence and ball-handling of Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young. It is a backcourt that combines outside shooting, court vision, and control of the pace.

Under the rim, the strength is just as intimidating. Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Aliyah Boston, and Angel Reese make up an interior front that dominates the boards and punishes in the paint. Added to names like Kahleah Copper and Rhyne Howard, the U.S. rotation barely loses any level when the substitutions come off the bench.

The Czech Republic's strong players

On the Czech side, the most internationally recognized reference is Eliška Joklová, a 24-year-old point guard who plays for the Minnesota Lynx in the WNBA, which gives her top-level experience against this kind of opponent. Shooting guard Petra Holešínská brings European experience from Turkey's Emlak Konut, while Julie Pospíšilová and Gabriela Andělová round out a perimeter that will have to carry a good part of the scoring load.

The key for Czechia will be efficiency from three-point range and not giving away the ball: against a team as athletic as the United States, every turnover turns into easy points in transition. If the Czechs can extend their possessions and draw the United States into a controlled-tempo game, they will at least have the chance to stay close.

What's at stake in Group D for the FIBA Women's World Cup

The group picture is revealing. The United States leads with 4 points, followed by Italy (1-1, 3 points) and China (1-1, 3 points), with Czechia (0-2, 2 points) closing the table. In the other matchup of the day, Italy and China face off in a direct duel for second place.

An American victory would all but seal the top spot in the group and put the Americans on track for a favorable position heading into the knockout stage. For Czechia, the margin is minimal: a third defeat would leave them depending on other results and on a points differential that currently works against them.

Players to watch in USA vs Czechia

Caitlin Clark (USA): her shooting range and her ability to speed up the game can open the scoring from the first quarter.

Breanna Stewart (USA): the versatility of the New York Liberty power forward is the engine both on offense and defense.

Eliška Joklová (Czechia): the only Czech representative in the WNBA will be responsible for directing the offense and maintaining her national team's competitiveness.

Prediction for the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup game between USA vs Czechia

Everything points to a United States victory, and by a wide margin. The +36 differential over two games, the depth of the bench, and the physical superiority make it hard to imagine anything other than dominance from start to finish.

Czechia, forced to take risks, may have streaks of outside shooting accuracy that make the scoreline look better, but keeping up the pace for 40 minutes against this U.S. roster is a huge task. The matchup at Berlin's Uber Arena should end with the Americans securing their third consecutive win and strengthening their hold on first place in Group D.

articles.title: Breanna Stewart powers Team USA to dominant win over Czechia after Italy scare
articles.standfirst: After a tough battle against Italy, the Americans bounced back in dominant fashion against Czechia.
articles.summary: After a tough battle against Italy, the Americans bounced back in dominant fashion against Czechia.
articles.body:
B reanna Stewart had 19 points, seven rebounds and six assists to help the United States rout the Czech Republic 105-64 on Monday.

The Americans rebounded from their worst preliminary-round game in 50 years after edging Italy 55-52 on Sunday. Stewart set the tone early to make sure that wouldn't happen again as the U.S. won its 33rd in a row in the tournament , going back to a semifinal loss to Russia in the 2006 World Cup.

Next up for the U.S. is the quarterfinal round on Thursday . They’ll face the winner of the Hungary vs. Japan game which takes place Tuesday.

Stewart had 11 points in the first 10 minutes as the U.S. jumped out to a 29-15 lead. The Americans had only 30 points in the first half against Italy. They kept it going in the second quarter behind Napheesa Collier, who had seven of her 12 points in the period.

The Americans extended the advantage to 57-33 at the half. They weren't challenged in the second half by the Czechs as the lead ballooned to more than 40 points.

Stewart finished short of her World Cup career-high of 23 points set against China in 2018. She only played just over 16 minutes against the Czechs. Stewart sat in the fourth quarter giving her no chance at becoming only the second player in World Cup history to have a triple double. The Czech's Erika Dobrovicova accomplished the feat in 1994 against Spain.

The Czech Republic finished winless in pool play. The Czechs were playing in their first World Cup since 2014. They won the silver medal when they hosted the event in 2010.

In other games on Monday, China beat Italy; Germany topped Mali; Belgium beat Australia; Puerto Rico edged Turkey; France routed Nigeria; Spain beat Japan and Hungary slipped past Korea.

articles.standfirst: Whatever tension existed between the two appears to be taking a back seat as Team USA chases gold
articles.summary: Whatever tension existed between the two appears to be taking a back seat as Team USA chases gold
articles.body:
When Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers were called up to represent the United States at the Basketball World Cup, many fans immediately went back to a moment when the two had a heated exchange during the Indiana Fever’s game against the Dallas Wings . Clark lost her temper during the moment, while Bueckers appeared to tell her to calm down.

Clark was not entering the tournament without previous tension . She already has a rivalry with Angel Reese, one of the players she has been most closely linked to because of the competition created by fans. Now, she also had an awkward moment in her history with Bueckers , who happens to be one of Reese’s closest friends on Team USA.

But their history has not stopped them from finding common ground

Those kinds of tensions can be difficult to ignore when young players, who could also be described as still maturing, have the responsibility of representing their country in such an important tournament . However, one moment showed that Clark and Bueckers are on the same page , working together toward the same goal: winning gold.

The two players also share similar paths to the WNBA. Both were selected first overall in their respective draft classes, and both went on to win WNBA Rookie of the Year honors. They have plenty in common, making it hard to imagine them carrying any real animosity toward each other, and seeing them work together has been a relief for fans.

The fans already have a name for the duo: Caige

Ahead of their game of the tournament, the two playmakers shared a fun exchange on the court . articles.title: When is the next Team USA game at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup? Date, time and opponent for next round
articles.summary: Team USA earned something increasingly valuable at the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup and that is time.
articles.body:
Team USA earned something increasingly valuable at the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup and that is time.

After completing the group stage unbeaten and securing first place in Group D, the defending champions advanced directly to the quarterfinals and avoided the additional elimination game facing teams that finished second or third.

The United States will next play on Thursday, September 10, in Berlin , with its quarterfinal opponent coming from Hungary or Japan . Those teams meet Tuesday in the Qualification to the Quarter-Finals round, with the winner moving immediately into USA’s side of the bracket.

FIBA is yet to confirm tipoff time for the American quarterfinal at the time of writing. That gives Kara Lawson ’s team a useful break after three games in four days and removes one potential obstacle from its pursuit of a fifth consecutive world championship.

Team USA earned direct path into quarterfinals

The Americans completed their preliminary schedule Monday with a 105-64 win over Czechia , finishing Group D at 3-0.

That followed a commanding opening victory against China and a much tougher 55-52 win over Italy , a game that tested USA considerably more than its other group-stage appearances.

Under the expanded 16-team format being used in Berlin, only the four group winners move directly into the last eight.

Teams finishing second and third must play another single-elimination game on September 8 or 9, while the fourth-place teams are eliminated. All four quarterfinals are then scheduled for Thursday, September 10 .

USA therefore gets to watch Tuesday’s Hungary-Japan matchup knowing its next opponent will have had to survive an additional knockout game.

Hungary and Japan offer very different potential tests

Hungary and Japan tip off at 5:45 p.m. local time in Berlin on Tuesday, September 8, which is 11:45 a.m. ET. The winner advances to face the United States.

Hungary ’s strength has largely come inside, particularly through Dorka Juhasz , while Japan offers a contrasting challenge built around pace and perimeter shooting.

Japan demonstrated just how dangerous that shooting can become in its 102-97 group-stage victory over Mali, when Saki Hayashi set a Women’s World Cup record by making nine three-pointers.

Either matchup would represent the beginning of the win-or-go-home portion of USA’s tournament. The Americans entered Berlin seeking their fifth straight Women’s World Cup crown and 12th overall.

Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese are among the players making their senior World Cup debuts, while USA is again trying to extend a run of dominance that stretches back through the previous four editions.

If the United States wins Thursday, its semifinal will be played Saturday, September 12, with the championship and bronze-medal games scheduled for Sunday, September 13.

First, though, USA can enjoy the advantage it earned by winning its group and a place in the quarterfinals without having to play again until Thursday.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese show off growing chemistry leaving fans buzzing
articles.standfirst: The former rivals are showing what they can do when they share the court
articles.summary: The former rivals are showing what they can do when they share the court
articles.body:
B asketball is also part of the entertainment world, and the rivalries and connections within the sport only add more to the competition. ​ ​One of the most talked-about rivalries in the WNBA since both players made it to the league, and one that already drew plenty of attention during their college careers, is the one between Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark.

Their matchups have always been closely followed, while the media and social media have also fueled the idea of a rivalry between them . Now, however, as teammates during the FIBA World Cup, the young players are showing that their rivalry does not mean they are enemies.

A different dynamic on the same side

During one of their games, Clark and Reese showed that the chemistry is there and that they can make each other better on the court . Reese said some time ago that she was sure they would eventually share a jersey, and now they are showing that they can coordinate and trust each other.

The win over Czechia provided another example of that connection. The FIBA World Cup page shared a clip of a fantastic lob pass from Clark to Reese, which led to an easy layup for Team USA . Clark’s pass to Reese quickly had fans buzzing.

Fans are getting more of the duo they wanted to see

Both players came off the bench and showed their connection on the court, leaving fans wanting more from the duo . Their performances also reflected their individual contributions, with Clark finishing the game with nine points and seven assists in 22 minutes of action, while Reese had 13 points on 4-of-5 shooting and six rebounds.

Fans loved seeing another example of the connection between Clark and Reese play out on the court , adding another moment to the growing story of what these two can do when they are on the same team.
